name: Crunchbase
data_types: Company profiles/firmographics, funding rounds, investors and funds, acquisitions (acquirer/target/price/date/type), IPOs, people/executives and founders, news signals, advanced financials, risk indicators, and proprietary predictive scores. Crunchbase publicly markets 7 prediction models including an ACQUISITION prediction and an IPO prediction - i.e. it already sells a product conceptually similar to the model JCAI wants to build.
coverage_geo: Global, strongest in US/Europe tech and VC-backed private companies. Public claims range 3M+ companies (about.crunchbase.com/data) to 4M+ private-company search (third-party ZoomInfo page). Asia/Japan coverage exists but is skewed to VC-funded startups; traditional Japanese SME/succession targets are largely absent. INFERRED: weak for Japanese mid-market non-tech.
history_depth: Not published as a single date. Practically ~2007 onward for dense coverage (Crunchbase launched 2007), sparser earlier. INFERRED, not confirmed on any official page.
api: yes - REST. Free/Basic API tier is DISCONTINUED (data.crunchbase.com states 'We are no longer offering our Basic API'). Full API requires an Enterprise or Applications licence. Documented rate limit 200 calls/minute. Docs: https://data.crunchbase.com/docs/using-the-api . An MCP server also exists.
bulk_delivery: yes (Enterprise / Data Licensing only) - bulk data exports plus custom data feeds; Snowflake integration referenced on the API product page. Seat plans have hard CSV export caps (2,000 rows/mo Pro, 5,000 rows/mo Business per third-party ZoomInfo page).
pricing: Seat plans, third-party sources, observed Sept 2026: Free $0; Pro $49/user/month billed annually (~$588/yr) or $99/month monthly; Business from ~$199/month (quote required); contact-credit add-ons $29-$99/month. API and Data Licensing are QUOTE ONLY with no public price and no published per-call metering. Third-party commentary (vendr.com, pipeline.zoominfo.com) states Enterprise contracts 'typically start around USD 50,000/yr' - THIRD-PARTY ESTIMATE, not confirmed by Crunchbase. Sources: https://pipeline.zoominfo.com/sales/crunchbase-pricing , https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/crunchbase .
ml_training_license: NEGATIVE / BLOCKING as standard. Crunchbase Terms of Service prohibit using the Content to train models, including generative AI technologies, with violation grounds for termination. Their MCP overview article puts the burden on the customer for 'restrictions related to model training, fine-tuning, persistent embeddings, data retention, or third-party AI tools'. A bespoke Data Licensing agreement would have to explicitly carve out ML training rights; assume extra cost and negotiation. Historic CC BY-NC 4.0 route covers non-commercial use only. CONFIRMED restriction; the carve-out possibility is INFERRED.
update_frequency: Continuous / daily; company claims 30M+ verified updates per year.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Structurally an excellent training set - it links companies, funding, ownership and acquisition events, exactly the label-plus-feature structure a target-prediction model needs. Two hard blockers: the ToS explicitly forbid model training absent a licensing carve-out, and Japanese non-tech SME coverage (JCAI's core market) is thin.
budget_tier: enterprise (>$50k/yr) for API/data licensing; low (<$10k/yr) for seat-only Pro/Business, which does NOT permit training
confidence: high on the ToS training prohibition and seat pricing; medium on API/licensing price level (third-party estimate); low on Japan coverage depth

name: Dealroom.co
data_types: Startup/scaleup and public company profiles, VC funding rounds, valuations, cap tables and shareholder structure, exits/M&A and acquirer activity, investors and funds, founder and operator profiles (18M+), revenue estimates and verified ARR, patent filings, ecosystem/sector taxonomies, stealth-company detection.
coverage_geo: Global with a strong Europe focus. Official figures (dealroom.co/our-data, observed Sept 2026): 3.6M+ companies tracked (3M+ cited on the API page), 336,000+ VC rounds since 2018, 256,000+ seed-to-Series-A rounds, 100,000+ investor funds, 18M+ people profiles, 76,278 startups detected in 2025, partnerships with 100+ government agencies. APAC/Japan: dataset is strongest for VC-funded tech; a third-party APAC-focused review (amafi.ai) states Dealroom's APAC SME / family-business / succession coverage is materially incomplete. Japan-specific counts not published.
history_depth: Funding-round counts are quoted 'since 2018', implying dense structured coverage from ~2018 with thinner history before. M&A/exit history depth not published - UNKNOWN.
api: yes - REST with OAuth2, plus a hosted MCP server for natural-language querying. Docs gated at https://docs.dealroom.co/docs/premium-api (request access via team@dealroom.co). Rate limits not public. Requires a separate API licence agreement with Dealroom.co on top of a platform plan.
bulk_delivery: yes - scheduled bulk data feeds, Snowflake, and CRM connectors (Salesforce, Affinity, HubSpot).
pricing: No official public price list; all quote-based. THIRD-PARTY REVIEW-SITE figures only (ellty.com, coldiq.com, tomba.io; observed 2026): Starter ~EUR 12,000/yr (up to 3 seats), Team ~EUR 20,000/yr (up to 6 seats), Corporate ~EUR 40,000/yr (up to 20 seats), Enterprise estimated EUR 35,000-50,000/yr. Premium plans include up to 10,000 exports per user. API is a SEPARATE line item on top, and reviewers report a clear price step for it. None of these amounts is published by Dealroom.
ml_training_license: LIKELY BLOCKING as standard. Dealroom ToS Art. 3.3 prohibits users from 'commercialise, share, copy, extract, or sub-license any of the data'; Art. 18.5 prohibits publishing raw datasets, modifying data and sub-licensing; Art. 17.7 prohibits scraping and excessive usage; Art. 18.1 limits free-account data to personal use. The ToS do NOT mention ML/AI training explicitly - that is a gap - but bulk extraction into a training corpus falls under the extraction/commercialisation prohibitions. A separate API/data licence with explicit training rights would be required. CONFIRMED clauses; application to ML is INFERRED.
update_frequency: Continuous; new-company detection claimed on filing or launch day. Bulk feeds delivered on a schedule.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Good feature richness (cap tables, shareholder structure, ARR estimates, exits) with a clean API/Snowflake path. But the universe is VC/tech-centric, APAC SME coverage is weak for a Japanese mid-market intermediary, and the EUR 12k-50k entry with API priced as an extra pushes it to the top of or beyond the stated budget.
budget_tier: mid ($10k-50k/yr) at best, likely enterprise (>$50k/yr) once API/bulk rights are added
confidence: high on coverage numbers and ToS text; low on pricing (third-party review sites only)

name: Tracxn
data_types: Private company profiles, funding rounds, investors, ACQUISITIONS as a first-class dataset (acquirer, target, deal date, acquisition type, disclosed deal value, links to public sources), valuations, sector/market taxonomies, deal-flow CRM, live deals, news, custom reports.
coverage_geo: Global. Official figures on tracxn.com/pricing (observed Sept 2026): 7.7M+ companies, 290K+ investors, 1.8M+ funding rounds, 226K+ acquisitions. The Acquisitions Database product page states 200K+ acquisitions. Asia is a relative strength (Indian company, heavy APAC emphasis). Japan: Tracxn's own Japan geography page cites 52,300+ Japanese startups and 1,210 acquisitions, so Japan deal depth is modest.
history_depth: Not published. INFERRED dense from roughly the 2010s onward, consistent with a startup-tracking origin. Not confirmed.
api: yes - token-authenticated API; endpoint catalogue published as Postman documentation covering companies, funding, acquisitions, investors and news. Max 20 records per call with pagination. Rate limits exist but exact numbers sit in a separate gated doc. API tokens generally do not expire on live accounts. Docs: https://help.tracxn.com/en/articles/8512359-getting-started-with-tracxn-apis . REST is implied by the docs structure but not explicitly stated.
bulk_delivery: yes - 'Data Solutions Packs' explicitly offer APIs and DATA DUMPS, in Full Access (all company data) or Limited Access (customised data points/datasets) configurations. Formats not published; CSV/Excel exports available in-product.
pricing: Lite tier is FREE for personal use (single seat, usage-limited exports/reports/alerts) and still displays the full coverage counts, which makes it usable for evaluation. Premium is 'Contact Sales' with no public number. Data Solutions Packs are priced by VOLUME OF UNIQUE COMPANIES ACCESSED on an annual contract, with no re-charge for repeat access to the same company; custom low-frequency high-cycle pricing exists for pipeline-enrichment use cases; 5-7 day PoC trials offered; discounts for non-profits and new ventures. Third-party sites (capterra.com, crozdesk.com, saasworthy.com) cite platform pricing 'from ~USD 550/month' - THIRD-PARTY figure, not on tracxn.com.
ml_training_license: UNKNOWN. No public statement on ML/AI training rights was found. The unique-company-count pricing model plus explicit data dumps and custom dataset packs suggest a negotiable data-licence posture, but this MUST be confirmed in writing with Tracxn sales/legal.
update_frequency: Continuous/daily in-platform; Data Solutions Packs can be configured for low-frequency, high-cycle refresh.
fit_for_lead_prediction: One of the best value-for-money candidates in this group: 226K+ acquisition records plus 7.7M company profiles, explicit data-dump and API packs, volume-based rather than seat-based pricing, and an Asia-leaning research team. Japan depth (~1,210 acquisitions) is too thin to be the sole Japanese signal but works as global training data plus Asia cross-border features. Worth an RFQ for a Limited Access pack scoped to acquisitions plus company attributes.
budget_tier: unknown - plausibly mid ($10k-50k/yr) for a scoped Limited Access data pack (INFERRED); enterprise if full 7.7M-company access is required
confidence: high on coverage counts and delivery model; low on price and on ML licence terms

name: Moody's / Bureau van Dijk - Orbis M&A (formerly Zephyr) plus Orbis
hq_country: Netherlands / Belgium (Bureau van Dijk); owned by Moody's (USA)
data_types: Orbis M&A (Zephyr): M&A deals AND RUMOURS, IPOs, private equity and venture rounds, joint ventures, share buybacks - with acquirer/target/vendor identities, deal value, stake percentages, deal status, deal rationale, ADVISORS on both sides, and pre-deal / post-deal / forecast MULTIPLES and financials. Directly linked to Orbis for company data: ownership structures and beneficial owners, financial statements, executives and directors, industry codes and scores. This is the richest structured M&A schema in the group. Notably there is no deal-value or size threshold for inclusion, unlike SDC.
coverage_geo: Global. Deal counts cited by university library sources: ~1.6M deals and rumours with 100,000+ added per year (Aalto), and ~2.3M deals and rumours in a more recent citation. Orbis company universe is very large (hundreds of millions of companies) with genuinely deep private-company and Japanese coverage sourced from local filings. Best Japan/Asia private-company depth of any provider in this group.
history_depth: Pan-European transactions from 1997; US deals from 2001. CONFIRMED via multiple independent library sources.
api: yes - Orbis API plus 'Catalysts' and industry connectors; also web interface and batch download. Access is via a licensed Moody's/BvD contract; developer docs are not public and rate limits are not published.
bulk_delivery: yes - Moody's explicitly markets bulk feeds, cloud delivery and real-time delivery for Orbis. Formats not published publicly.
pricing: QUOTE ONLY. No public price points at all and no free tier. INFERRED from market practice that a commercial Orbis + Orbis M&A licence carrying API/bulk rights sits well above USD 50k/yr - NOT confirmed, and no public figure was found. Do not quote a number.
ml_training_license: UNKNOWN, but Moody's/BvD run a formal data-licensing business and routinely negotiate redistribution and derived-data rights, so an ML-training carve-out is a normal commercial conversation. Standard seat-based subscriptions would not permit corpus building. Requires legal review by a qualified adviser.
language: English output; underlying company data sourced from local-language filings including Japanese, normalised to English.
update_frequency: Daily/continuous deal additions; company financials on filing cycles.
fit_for_lead_prediction: The single best-fit dataset in this group on content quality: real deal labels back to 1997, advisors, multiples, rationale, no size threshold, plus ownership and financials for the target universe, and unmatched Japanese private-company depth - which is exactly what a JCAI target-prediction model needs. The blocker is cost and licence structure, not data. Recommend pricing it even if it exceeds budget, and asking specifically for a scoped historical bulk extract (Japan plus APAC deals, plus Orbis company attributes) rather than full-platform access.
confidence: high on data content and history depth; low on pricing and licence terms

name: Mergr
data_types: PE firms and their portfolio companies, M&A / change-of-control transactions, late-stage financings, company profiles, M&A ADVISORS and advisor mandates, PE/M&A contacts (people), official press announcements. Deals searchable by date, buyer, seller, target, sector, deal value, transaction type, side and geography. All data is human-researched in-house with NO third-party databases licensed or aggregated - unusually clean provenance for onward licensing.
coverage_geo: Global but US/Europe mid-market focused. Official counts on mergr.com/pricing (observed Sept 2026): 4,900+ PE firms, 86,000+ PE/M&A contacts, 225,000+ transactions, 225,000+ companies, 3,900+ M&A advisors. (A docs page still cites ~184K transactions - an older figure.) Cross-border search is supported. Asia/Japan coverage is NOT published and is INFERRED weak relative to US/Europe.
api: yes - 'Mergr API', key-authenticated live API querying firms, companies, deals, advisors and professionals. Sold as part of the separate 'Data Direct' product, not included in Pro. No public developer docs URL found; scoping happens after a sales conversation, so rate limits are unknown. Separately, an AI Connector (ChatGPT / Claude / Perplexity) is included on the Pro seat plan.
bulk_delivery: yes - 'Mergr Exports': custom CSV/Excel files, one-time pull or recurring refresh, importable into CRM, models and workflows. SFTP, S3 and Snowflake are not mentioned.
pricing: PUBLIC and cheap for seats: Mergr Pro USD 150/month with a 7-day free trial; annual billing available (annual amount not published); 250-record export cap on Pro; 'Pro for Teams' is custom-quoted. Data Direct (API plus bulk exports) is QUOTE ONLY, priced by data scope and volume and billed independently of Mergr membership. Sources: https://mergr.com/pricing , https://mergr.com/data (observed Sept 2026). Their own comparison article describes PitchBook as 'expensive ($25K+/user/year typical)' - that is Mergr's characterisation of a competitor, not their own price.
ml_training_license: UNKNOWN - not addressed on the Data Direct page, which points to https://mergr.com/terms . However, because Mergr owns 100% of its data with no upstream licensors, it has more freedom than aggregators to grant ML-training rights. INFERRED to be the most negotiable vendor in this group on training rights. Must be confirmed in writing.
update_frequency: Daily - research team publishes new transactions, profiles and advisor involvement every day.
fit_for_lead_prediction: The strongest budget-fit candidate: ~225K human-verified transactions with buyers, sellers, targets and advisors, sold as scoped bulk exports, from a vendor that owns its data outright and prices at the low end. Main weakness is Asia/Japan coverage, so treat it as a source of clean global deal labels and PE-buyer behaviour features rather than Japanese lead data. Worth a direct RFQ for a full historical transaction plus company extract.
budget_tier: low (<$10k/yr) for seats; INFERRED low-to-mid for a scoped Data Direct extract - not confirmed
confidence: high on seat pricing and record counts; low on Data Direct price, history depth, Asia coverage and licence terms

name: Intellizence
data_types: News-signal-derived M&A and divestiture dataset with 16+ data points per deal: unique deal ID, announced date, last-modified date; acquirer, acquired and divesting company names plus domain, industry, HQ location, company type and ticker; deal amount and currency; deal status; deal type; source news or press-release title and URL. Adjacent signal datasets also sold (startup funding, layoffs, business expansion, alliances and partnerships, regulatory, company and industry news) which are useful leading indicators of M&A propensity.
coverage_geo: Global - marketing material cites deals across 140+ countries with multi-currency deal-value tracking, public and private companies. Asia/Japan specifics not published. INFERRED weak on Japanese-language-only domestic deals because the pipeline is English-language news driven.
history_depth: SHALLOW, and the two official sources DISAGREE: the API docs state data from 1 January 2020 onward, while the product page states 'January 2021 onwards'. Either way only about 5-6 years of history, which is a real limitation for training a time-series model.
api: yes - documented REST API. Base URL https://connect.intellizence.com , endpoint POST /api/dataset/mna , auth via x-api-key HTTP header. Filters on date, company name/domain (partial match supported), industry, location, company type, deal type, deal status and deal amount; comma-separated or array multi-values; limit parameter. Two retrieval modes: ANNOUNCED (default) and LAST-MODIFIED (recommended for daily incremental pulls). Webhooks supported. Consumption can be credit-metered - remaining credit balance is returned in responses. Rate limits not published. Docs: https://docs.intellizence.com/signals-api/mergers-and-acquisitions
bulk_delivery: partial - delivered via web app and REST API; also distributed through AWS Data Exchange, Canada's Open Data Exchange (ODX) and Clay, and integrates with Salesforce and HubSpot. CSV, S3 and Snowflake are NOT mentioned on their own pages.
pricing: QUOTE ONLY. The company says 'flexible pricing'; Datarade's auto-generated profile explicitly states 'Intellizence has not published pricing information for their data services'. Free trial and demo offered. No public amounts found - do not estimate.
ml_training_license: UNKNOWN - not addressed publicly. Their positioning as a data-products company distributing via AWS Data Exchange, plus a 'Deep Learning (DL) Data' category tag on their Datarade profile, suggests ML buyers are an expected persona and training rights are likely negotiable. Not confirmed.
update_frequency: Daily refresh; typical lag of 1 to 2 business days from public announcement.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Useful as a cheap-to-integrate, well-documented source of RECENT deal labels plus adjacent leading signals (funding, expansion, layoffs, partnerships), and the LAST-MODIFIED mode makes incremental ingestion easy. But only 2020/2021 onward and news-derived, so it cannot supply the long historical label series a robust target-prediction model wants, nor deep Japanese domestic coverage. Good complement, poor foundation.
budget_tier: unknown - INFERRED low-to-mid based on SME/mid-market data-product positioning; no public price
confidence: high on API mechanics and history start date; medium on coverage claims; low on pricing and licence

name: Financial Modeling Prep (FMP)
data_types: Listed-company financial data: financial statements (30+ years on higher tiers), ratios, valuations, prices, corporate actions, earnings, IPO calendar, ESG, news - plus two dedicated M&A endpoints: 'Latest Mergers & Acquisitions' and 'Search Mergers & Acquisitions' (by company name). The M&A endpoints are SEC-filing-derived and therefore thin: transaction date, company names and a link to the underlying filing. No advisors, no multiples, no deal rationale, no private-target detail.
coverage_geo: Global equity markets for prices and fundamentals (broad exchange coverage including Tokyo), but the M&A endpoints are effectively US SEC-filing centric. INFERRED negligible coverage of Japanese domestic private-company M&A. Not usable as a Japan/Asia deal source.
history_depth: Financial statements 5+ years on Starter, 30+ years on Premium and Ultimate. M&A endpoint history depth is NOT published - UNKNOWN.
api: yes - REST, very well documented and developer-friendly, self-serve keys. Docs: https://site.financialmodelingprep.com/developer/docs/stable/latest-mergers-acquisitions and .../search-mergers-acquisitions . Rate limits by plan (see pricing). An MCP server also exists. IMPORTANT GAP: which plan unlocks the M&A endpoints is NOT stated publicly and must be confirmed before purchase.
bulk_delivery: partial - bulk/batch endpoints exist for fundamentals on higher tiers; no SFTP, S3 or Snowflake delivery advertised. INFERRED you would paginate the API and persist it yourself.
pricing: PUBLIC and very cheap, but sources disagree and the official pricing page returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch. Third-party reads of that page, observed Sept 2026: (a) Free $0 at 250 calls per DAY; Starter $22/mo at 300 calls/min; Premium $59/mo at 750 calls/min; Ultimate $149/mo at 3,000 calls/min [qveris.ai, annual-billing prices]. (b) Starter $29/mo, Premium $69/mo, Ultimate $139/mo month-to-month, with annual billing at $264 / $708 / $1,788 per year and up to 34% annual discount [trustradius.com, findmymoat.com]. Either way roughly USD 250-1,800 per year. Currency USD.
ml_training_license: PARTIALLY RESTRICTED. Personal/standard plans are for individual use; DISPLAY or REDISTRIBUTION of FMP data requires a separate 'Data Display and Licensing Agreement' / commercial agreement. Internal-only ML training is not explicitly addressed in public material - arguably not 'display or redistribution', but that is an interpretation, NOT a confirmed permission. Confirm in writing; the commercial licence is likely still inexpensive relative to the rest of this list.
update_frequency: Real-time to daily depending on endpoint; the M&A endpoint tracks new filings.
fit_for_lead_prediction: The cheapest way to obtain a machine-readable M&A event feed plus listed-company fundamentals, and the fundamentals are genuinely useful acquirer-side features (cash, leverage, growth, valuation multiples). But the M&A records themselves are thin, SEC-centric and lack Japanese private-deal coverage, so FMP is a low-cost fundamentals/feature layer, not the deal-label source.
budget_tier: low (<$10k/yr) - roughly USD 264 to USD 1,788 per year
confidence: high that it is cheap and has M&A endpoints; medium on exact price (official page blocked, third-party figures conflict); low on M&A history depth and on which tier unlocks the endpoints

name: Other low-cost finance APIs screened for M&A (EOD Historical Data / EODHD, Polygon.io, Finnhub)
hq_country: EODHD: UK/France; Polygon.io: USA; Finnhub: USA
data_types: Prices (EOD and intraday), fundamentals, corporate actions (splits, dividends), earnings, IPO calendars, macro calendars, news and news sentiment. CONFIRMED NEGATIVE on the key requirement: no dedicated mergers-and-acquisitions endpoint was found for any of the three. M&A-adjacent signals only - IPO calendars, corporate actions, delisting events, and news sentiment that could be mined for deal announcements (a build, not a dataset).
coverage_geo: EODHD: global, 150,000+ tickers across many exchanges including Tokyo. Polygon.io: primarily US equities, options, FX and crypto. Finnhub: global equities plus news. All three are listed-security universes with effectively zero private-company coverage - which is where Japanese M&A targets live.
history_depth: EODHD: decades of EOD history (30+ years on many tickers). Polygon: 20+ years US. Finnhub: varies by endpoint. Not applicable to M&A events, since none carries an M&A dataset.
api: yes - all three are REST, well documented and self-serve with free tiers. But no M&A endpoint. Among the cheap finance APIs, only FMP surfaced explicit mergers-acquisitions endpoints.
bulk_delivery: yes - EODHD offers bulk EOD and bulk fundamentals downloads (CSV); Polygon offers flat files via S3. Neither includes M&A deal data.
pricing: All three publish public self-serve pricing, typically in the range of roughly USD 20-250 per month per plan, with free tiers. EXACT current amounts were NOT verified in this research pass - do not quote figures for these three.
ml_training_license: UNKNOWN per vendor and not verified. Market-data vendors typically restrict redistribution and require a commercial or derived-data licence.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Do NOT buy these for M&A events - they do not hold them. EODHD is worth a small spend purely as a cheap global listed-company fundamentals and Tokyo-exchange price/financials layer for building acquirer-capacity features. Recommend deprioritising Polygon.io and Finnhub entirely for this project.

name: Diffbot Knowledge Graph
data_types: Web-scale automatically-constructed knowledge graph. The Organization entity carries 150+ fields including directly M&A-relevant ones: acquiredBy (the organization that most recently acquired this organization), isAcquired (boolean), predecessors and successors (merger/consolidation lineage), investments (rounds received), totalInvestment, nbUniqueInvestors - plus subsidiaries, parent company, board members, founders, CEO, revenue and quarterly/yearly financials, capitalization, employee counts, locations, technologies used, NAICS/SIC/NACE codes and corporate registration/tax identifiers across 20+ jurisdictions. Also 1.6B+ articles for news signals.
coverage_geo: Global; 246M+ organizations claimed. Because it is built from web crawling plus registry data spanning 20+ jurisdictions of corporate IDs, Japanese company BREADTH is likely better than the VC-focused vendors, but Japanese DEAL-level detail will be shallow. Asia-specific counts not published.
history_depth: Not published. The graph is a current-state snapshot with entity-level provenance rather than a deal time series, and acquiredBy captures only the MOST RECENT acquirer - so historical deal sequences and prior owners are lost. This is the key structural weakness for training.
api: yes - REST (GET and POST), plus DQL (Diffbot Query Language) for knowledge-graph search, a Bulk Extract API, and official Python and TypeScript libraries. Rate limits by plan: Free 5 requests/min; Startup 5 requests/sec; Plus 25 requests/sec; Enterprise 25+ requests/sec. Docs: https://docs.diffbot.com/
bulk_delivery: partial - a Bulk Extract API exists and knowledge-graph entity export is metered at 25 credits per entity exported (100 credits per facet query). No SFTP, S3 or Snowflake firehose is advertised. Note the credit economics: at 25 credits per entity, the Plus plan's 1,000,000 credits/month yields only about 40,000 organization exports per month, so extracting a large training corpus is expensive in practice.
pricing: FULLY PUBLIC, observed Sept 2026 at https://www.diffbot.com/pricing : Free USD 0 with 10,000 credits/month at 5 req/min (a 14-day trial variant also grants 10,000 credits); Startup USD 299/month with 250,000 credits/month, overage USD 0.001/credit; Plus USD 899/month with 1,000,000 credits/month, overage USD 0.0009/credit, 25 active crawls, 3 seats; Enterprise custom with 2,000,000+ credits and overage USD 0.00085/credit. No long-term contract, monthly cancellation. Annualised: Startup about USD 3,588/yr, Plus about USD 10,788/yr.
ml_training_license: MOST PERMISSIVE IN THE GROUP, with a caveat. Diffbot's Terms of Use state 'you may display and use the facts generated by the Service as part of a commercial application', which reads as allowing internal derived use. Prohibited: 'sublicense, resell, rent, lease, transfer, assign, time share, or otherwise commercially exploit or make the Service available to any third party'. ML/AI training is NOT explicitly addressed either way, and no explicit retention or caching clause was found. Diffbot actively markets the KG as LLM grounding data and open-sources its own models, so the commercial posture is AI-friendly. Get written confirmation for training use. Quotes CONFIRMED; ML permission INFERRED.
language: English normalised output; crawls multilingual sources including Japanese.
update_frequency: Continuous crawling; no fixed published cycle.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Best value for the FEATURE side of the model: 246M organizations with financials, ownership, subsidiaries, executives, tech stack and registry IDs at USD 299-899/month with public pricing and a comparatively permissive commercial-use clause. But it is a poor LABEL source - acquiredBy holds only the latest acquirer with no reliable deal value or date and no advisor detail, so a proper historical deal panel cannot be reconstructed from it. Pair Diffbot (features) with a real deal database (labels).
budget_tier: low (<$10k/yr) at Startup; mid ($10k-50k/yr) at Plus or with heavy entity-export volume
confidence: high on pricing, fields and rate limits; medium on ToS interpretation for ML training; low on Japan depth

name: S&P Capital IQ Pro - enterprise / likely out of budget
data_types: M&A transactions, public and private company financials, ownership, executives, estimates, credit, industry data, screening, advisors, multiples. S&P Global also runs a substantial standalone data-feed business (Xpressfeed) and a cloud/marketplace delivery line.
